questions.stem: India's FIRST INDIVIDUAL OLYMPIC GOLD MEDAL was won by:

options.option_text: ABHINAV BINDRA — 10m Air Rifle, BEIJING 2008; broke India’s 28-year individual-gold drought

questions.explanation: ABHINAV BINDRA (b. 1982, Dehradun; raised in Chandigarh) — won India's FIRST EVER INDIVIDUAL OLYMPIC GOLD MEDAL at BEIJING OLYMPICS 2008 (11 Aug 2008) in MEN'S 10m AIR RIFLE shooting. Scored 700.5 points in qualification + final. Prior to this, India's only Olympic GOLDS were TEAM golds in FIELD HOCKEY (8 golds from 1928-1980). NEERAJ CHOPRA (Javelin) later became the FIRST ATHLETICS Olympic gold at TOKYO 2020 (held Aug 2021) — 87.58 m. INDIVIDUAL OLYMPIC MEDALS (pre-Bindra): (1) NORMAN PRITCHARD (1900 Paris, 2 silvers — but debated whether he represented India or Britain); (2) KD JADHAV (1952 Helsinki, Wrestling Bantamweight BRONZE — India’s first individual Olympic medal of independent India); (3) LEANDER PAES (1996 Atlanta, Tennis Singles BRONZE); (4) KARNAM MALLESWARI (2000 Sydney, Weightlifting BRONZE — 1st Indian woman to win an Olympic medal); (5) RAJYAVARDHAN SINGH RATHORE (2004 Athens, Double Trap shooting SILVER — 1st individual silver); (6) Abhinav Bindra 2008 GOLD. Bindra received the KHEL RATNA in 2001 (youngest then). Padma Bhushan 2009. Retired in 2016 after Rio.

questions.stem: The FIVE RINGS of the Olympic symbol represent:

options.option_text: The FIVE INHABITED CONTINENTS of the world
The 5 modern Olympic Games chronological eras

questions.explanation: OLYMPIC SYMBOL (5 interlocking rings) — designed in 1913 by PIERRE DE COUBERTIN (father of the modern Olympic movement) on the OLYMPIC FLAG. RINGS = FIVE inhabited CONTINENTS (in the old 5-continent model that merges Europe and combines North+South America, excluding Antarctica): AFRICA, AMERICAS, ASIA, EUROPE, OCEANIA. COLOURS = Blue, Yellow, Black, Green, Red on WHITE background. Chosen because AT LEAST ONE of these six colours appears on every NATIONAL FLAG in the world at that time. OLYMPIC MOTTO: ‘CITIUS, ALTIUS, FORTIUS — COMMUNITER’ (‘Faster, Higher, Stronger — Together’). ‘Communiter’ added in 2021 (previously just Citius-Altius-Fortius since 1894, coined by Father Henri Didon, adopted by Coubertin). OLYMPIC CREED: ‘The most important thing in the Olympic Games is not to win but to take part, just as the most important thing in life is not the triumph but the struggle’. OLYMPIC TORCH: ritual dates back to 1936 Berlin; flame kindled at Olympia, Greece from sun's rays; relayed to host city. OLYMPIC OATH: taken by an athlete of the host country. INTERNATIONAL OLYMPIC COMMITTEE (IOC) — formed 1894 in Paris by Coubertin; HQ LAUSANNE, Switzerland. First modern Olympics: ATHENS 1896. colours Blue-Yellow-Black-Green-Red were chosen so that AT LEAST ONE appears on every national flag of the world; Africa, Americas, Asia, Europe, Oceania.

questions.stem: India's FIRST TRACK & FIELD (athletics) Olympic gold was won by:

options.option_text: NEERAJ CHOPRA — JAVELIN THROW at TOKYO 2020 (held Aug 2021); winning throw 87.58 m

questions.explanation: NEERAJ CHOPRA (b. 24 Dec 1997, Khandra village, Panipat, Haryana) — won India's FIRST EVER OLYMPIC GOLD in ATHLETICS (track & field) at the delayed TOKYO 2020 OLYMPICS on 7 AUG 2021. EVENT: MEN'S JAVELIN THROW. Winning throw: 87.58 m on his 2nd attempt. This was ONLY INDIA's 2nd individual Olympic gold (first was Abhinav Bindra 2008 shooting). 23 years old at time of win. Previously: (1) 2016 World U20 (Junior) champion — 86.48 m (still a world junior record); (2) Commonwealth Games 2018 & 2022 GOLD; (3) Asian Games 2018 & 2022 GOLD; (4) Diamond League champion 2022, runner-up in others; (5) World Championships 2022 SILVER, 2023 GOLD (Budapest — India’s first World Athletics Championships gold); (6) PARIS 2024 OLYMPICS: SILVER (89.45 m — Arshad Nadeem of Pakistan took gold with 92.97 m, an Olympic record). Neeraj became the first Indian to throw 90+ m in 2025 (Doha DL, 90.23 m). AWARDS: Khel Ratna 2021, Padma Shri 2022, Honorary rank of Sub-Inspector → later Lt in Indian Army (Territorial). PREVIOUS INDIAN ATHLETICS MISSES: (1) Milkha Singh — 4th in 400 m at Rome 1960; (2) PT Usha — 4th in 400 m hurdles at LA 1984 (lost bronze by 1/100th of a second); (3) Anju Bobby George — 6th in Long Jump Athens 2004 (held bronze in World Championships 2003).

questions.stem: India's FIRST WOMAN to win an Olympic medal was:

options.option_text: KARNAM MALLESWARI — WEIGHTLIFTING BRONZE (69 kg class) at SYDNEY 2000; total lift 240 kg

questions.explanation: KARNAM MALLESWARI (b. 1 June 1975, Voosavanipeta village, Srikakulam district, ANDHRA PRADESH) — FIRST INDIAN WOMAN to win an OLYMPIC MEDAL. At SYDNEY 2000 OLYMPICS (19 Sep 2000), she won BRONZE in the WOMEN’S 69 kg weightlifting category; total lift 240 kg (110 kg snatch + 130 kg clean & jerk). She was beaten by Lin Weining (China, gold, 242.5 kg) and Ervel Krutzler (Hungary, silver, also 242.5 kg). Malleswari was also the 1994 & 1995 WORLD CHAMPION in 54 kg, 9-time national champion. Padma Shri 1999, Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna 1995-96, Arjuna Award 1994. SUBSEQUENT INDIAN WOMEN OLYMPIC MEDALISTS (chronologically): (2) MARY KOM — Boxing BRONZE 2012 London; (3) SAINA NEHWAL — Badminton BRONZE 2012 London (first Indian badminton medal); (4) PV SINDHU — Badminton SILVER 2016 Rio (1st Indian woman to win OLYMPIC SILVER), BRONZE 2020 Tokyo; (5) SAKSHI MALIK — Wrestling BRONZE 2016 (58 kg freestyle); (6) MIRABAI CHANU — Weightlifting SILVER 49 kg 2020 Tokyo; (7) LOVLINA BORGOHAIN — Boxing BRONZE 2020; (8) PV Sindhu — 2nd medal 2020 Tokyo; (9) MANU BHAKER — Shooting 2 BRONZES at Paris 2024 (1st Indian woman to win 2 medals at a single Olympics).

questions.stem: India has won the most OLYMPIC GOLDS in which sport?
questions.explanation: INDIAN FIELD HOCKEY at OLYMPICS — GOLDEN ERA 1928-1980; won 8 GOLDS, 1 SILVER (1960 Rome, lost to Pakistan 0-1), 3 BRONZES (1968, 1972, 2020 Tokyo, 2024 Paris — actually 2 bronzes in this modern era). GOLD YEARS: (1) 1928 AMSTERDAM — Dhyan Chand scoring spree; beat Netherlands 3-0; (2) 1932 LOS ANGELES — beat USA 24-1, Japan 11-1; (3) 1936 BERLIN — beat Germany (Nazi regime) 8-1 in final, Dhyan Chand scored 3; Hitler supposedly offered him Wehrmacht rank — he refused; (4) 1948 LONDON — first as independent India, beat UK 4-0; captain Kishan Lal; (5) 1952 HELSINKI — beat Netherlands 6-1; Balbir Singh Sr hat-trick; (6) 1956 MELBOURNE — Dhyan Chand retired by now; captain Balbir Singh Sr; (7) 1964 TOKYO — beat Pakistan 1-0; (8) 1980 MOSCOW — beat Spain 4-3; captain Vasudevan Bhaskaran. After 1980, hockey standards globally changed (astro-turf introduced 1970s = faster game; India slower to adapt); no medal till 2020 TOKYO BRONZE (beat Germany 5-4, ending 41-yr medal drought — captain Manpreet Singh, coach Graham Reid). 2024 PARIS — BRONZE again (beat Spain 2-1; captain Harmanpreet Singh). WOMEN’S TEAM: no Olympic medal yet (4th place Tokyo 2020). DHYAN CHAND (‘The Wizard’) = greatest Indian hockey player; National Sports Day 29 Aug (his birthday); Khel Ratna renamed ‘Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna’ 2021. 8 OLYMPIC GOLDS (1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, 1956, 1964, 1980); 11 total medals counting bronzes/silvers.

questions.stem: The HEADQUARTERS of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) is at:
questions.explanation: INTERNATIONAL OLYMPIC COMMITTEE (IOC) — the supreme authority of the OLYMPIC MOVEMENT. FOUNDED: 23 JUNE 1894 in PARIS by PIERRE DE COUBERTIN + DEMETRIOS VIKELAS (first President). HEADQUARTERS: LAUSANNE, Switzerland (moved from Paris in 1915 during WWI). MEMBER STRUCTURE: up to 115 active IOC members + honorary members. CURRENT PRESIDENT (as of 2026): KIRSTY COVENTRY (Zimbabwean, ex-swimmer, former IOC member, elected 2025 to succeed Thomas Bach; she is the first female + first African IOC President). Past Presidents: Coubertin (1896-1925), Avery Brundage (1952-72), Juan Antonio Samaranch (1980-2001), Jacques Rogge (2001-2013), Thomas Bach (2013-2025), Kirsty Coventry (2025-). THE OLYMPIC MUSEUM is in Lausanne (opened 1993). 23 JUNE = OLYMPIC DAY (anniversary of IOC founding). THREE PILLARS of Olympic Movement: IOC + International Federations (IFs, one per sport) + National Olympic Committees (NOCs, one per country — India’s is IOA, Indian Olympic Association, founded 1927). Olympic CHARTER — the governing document. OTHER KEY SPORTS HQ: FIFA (Zurich), ICC (Dubai), FINA (Lausanne), World Athletics (Monaco), BWF (Kuala Lumpur). since 1915, along the shore of Lake Geneva; hosts The Olympic Museum.

questions.stem: At the PARIS 2024 OLYMPICS, India won a total of:

options.option_text: 6 medals — 0 gold, 1 silver (Neeraj Chopra), 5 bronzes (hockey men, Swapnil Kusale, Sarabjot-Manu, Manu Bhaker, Aman Sehrawat)

questions.explanation: INDIA AT PARIS OLYMPICS 2024 — FINAL TALLY: 0 GOLDS, 1 SILVER, 5 BRONZES = 6 medals; RANKED 71st in medal table. LIST: (1) MANU BHAKER — BRONZE in Women's 10m Air Pistol (first medal of Paris for India; FIRST Indian woman to win an Olympic shooting medal); (2) MANU BHAKER + SARABJOT SINGH — BRONZE in 10m Air Pistol Mixed Team (Manu thus became the FIRST INDIAN woman to win 2 medals at a single Olympics, and first Indian since PV Sindhu to have 2 Olympic medals); (3) SWAPNIL KUSALE — BRONZE in Men's 50m Rifle 3 Positions; (4) INDIAN MEN'S HOCKEY TEAM — BRONZE (beat Spain 2-1 in 3rd-place playoff, captained by Harmanpreet Singh, goalie PR Sreejesh retiring); (5) NEERAJ CHOPRA — SILVER in Men's Javelin Throw (89.45 m, beaten by Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem's 92.97 m Olympic record); (6) AMAN SEHRAWAT — BRONZE in Men's Wrestling 57 kg (youngest Indian individual Olympic medallist, 21 years old). DISAPPOINTMENTS: Vinesh Phogat disqualified before gold medal final (100g overweight) — she appealed for joint silver, CAS rejected. INDIA sent its LARGEST-ever Olympic contingent — 117 athletes. India had set a target of 10+ medals based on Tokyo 7. PARIS 2024 medal table top: USA 126 (40G), CHINA 91 (40G, tied with USA for most golds but USA had more silvers), JAPAN, AUSTRALIA, FRANCE.

questions.stem: The next SUMMER OLYMPICS after Paris 2024 will be held in:

options.option_text: LOS ANGELES, USA (2028) — 34th Olympiad; LA will host for the 3rd time (1932, 1984, 2028)

questions.explanation: FUTURE OLYMPICS SCHEDULE (as of 2026): (1) SUMMER 2028 — LOS ANGELES, USA. 34th Olympiad; awarded 2017 in a double-allocation with Paris 2024. LA will be 3rd-time host (1932, 1984, 2028) — joining London (1908, 1948, 2012) as only cities to host 3 times. Venue for opening ceremony: LA Memorial Coliseum + SoFi Stadium. New sports: FLAG FOOTBALL (debut), CRICKET (returns after 128 years, T20 format, 6 teams — India qualifies likely), SQUASH (debut), BASEBALL+SOFTBALL (returns), LACROSSE (sixes). Breakdance (debuted Paris 2024) dropped. (2) WINTER 2026 — MILANO-CORTINA D'AMPEZZO, ITALY (6-22 Feb 2026). 25th Winter Olympiad. (3) SUMMER 2032 — BRISBANE, AUSTRALIA. Announced 2021; first time Australia hosts since Sydney 2000. Brisbane stadium: new Gabba redevelopment. (4) WINTER 2030 — FRENCH ALPS (awarded 2024). (5) SUMMER 2036 — BID process ongoing; INDIA (AHMEDABAD) has submitted a bid; other contenders: Istanbul (Turkey), Riyadh (Saudi Arabia), Doha (Qatar), Santiago (Chile), Warsaw (Poland). IOA formally submitted letter of intent 2024. PM Modi announced Ahmedabad bid at Mumbai IOC Session 2023. OTHER Olympic facts: (6) WINTER 2034 — SALT LAKE CITY, USA (announced 2024). YOUTH OLYMPICS: 2026 — Dakar (Senegal, first YOG in Africa).

questions.stem: The ancient Olympic Games of GREECE were held in honour of:
questions.explanation: ANCIENT OLYMPIC GAMES — religious+athletic festival held in honour of ZEUS (king of Greek gods) at OLYMPIA (not Mount Olympus!; Olympia is in the western Peloponnese, ancient region of Elis). Founded traditionally in 776 BCE (first recorded Olympiad); held every 4 YEARS for over 1,169 years until abolished by Roman Emperor THEODOSIUS I in 393 CE as a pagan festival (after Christianity became state religion). OLYMPIAD = 4-year interval; used as the primary Greek timekeeping method. FIRST-EVENT: STADION (short foot race ~192 m); winner: KOROIBOS of Elis (cook). Events expanded: wrestling, boxing, pentathlon, equestrian (horse, chariot), pankration. ATHLETES competed nude (gymnos, hence gymnasium) and were Greek-speaking FREE men (no slaves, no women until later). PRIZE: olive wreath (kotinos) — no cash. OLYMPIC TRUCE (ekecheiria): fighting suspended so athletes could travel safely. HERAEA — separate games for women in honour of Hera. MODERN REVIVAL: PIERRE DE COUBERTIN (French educator) championed revival; after lectures at Sorbonne 1892; congress of 1894 formed IOC; FIRST MODERN OLYMPICS held at ATHENS in 1896 (April 6-15). 13 countries, 280 athletes, 43 events; host Greece topped with 10 golds; USA second. First gold medallist of modern era: JAMES CONNOLLY (USA, Triple Jump). Since then, Olympic Games held every 4 years (exceptions: World Wars — 1916, 1940, 1944 cancelled; Tokyo 2020 postponed to 2021 due to COVID). father of Greek gods; held every 4 years at OLYMPIA (in Elis, western Peloponnese) from 776 BCE to 393 CE.

questions.stem: The PARA-OLYMPICS / PARALYMPIC GAMES are held for:

options.option_text: ATHLETES with PHYSICAL / VISUAL / INTELLECTUAL IMPAIRMENTS

questions.explanation: PARALYMPIC GAMES — major international multi-sport event for athletes with a range of DISABILITIES including impaired muscle power, limb deficiencies, vision impairment, intellectual impairments. NAME: ‘PARA’ = Greek ‘beside/alongside’ → games held alongside Olympics in same city. FOUNDED by Sir LUDWIG GUTTMANN (neurologist who treated spinal-cord patients at Stoke Mandeville hospital, UK) — organised the 1948 Stoke Mandeville Games for WWII veterans. 1960 ROME — first official Paralympic Games (held 6 days after Olympic closing); 400 athletes, 23 countries. Since 1988 SEOUL, Paralympics have been held in the SAME HOST CITY as the Olympics (and since 2012 London, using the same venues). Winter Paralympics began 1976 (Örnsköldsvik, Sweden). GOVERNING BODY: INTERNATIONAL PARALYMPIC COMMITTEE (IPC) — formed 1989, HQ BONN (Germany). Athletes are CLASSIFIED by impairment type & degree (e.g., T11 totally blind, T12 low vision, T13 best vision, etc.). PARALYMPIC MOTTO: ‘SPIRIT IN MOTION’. PARALYMPIC SYMBOL: 3 agitos (curved shapes — Latin ‘I move’); red, blue, green. INDIA AT PARALYMPICS — 29 all-time medals till PARIS 2024 (which alone gave India 29 medals incl. 7 GOLDS — best-ever; shooting & athletics dominant; AVANI LEKHARA defended 10m air rifle SH1 gold). Famous Indian para-athletes: DEVENDRA JHAJHARIA (javelin F46 — first Indian para-athlete to win TWO golds — Athens 2004 + Rio 2016), MARIYAPPAN THANGAVELU (high jump T63 gold Rio 2016), SUMIT ANTIL (javelin F64 gold Tokyo 2020 + Paris 2024), MANISH NARWAL, PRAVEEN KUMAR. SPECIAL OLYMPICS (separate, for intellectual disabilities) and DEAFLYMPICS are DIFFERENT events. held right after the Summer/Winter Olympics in the same host city; governed by the IPC (International Paralympic Committee, Bonn).
